title: make dev keeps its job worker running: a worker that ends is said loudly and started again
request: The owner defined a problem on Home, said build, and nothing ran: the Workflow page stayed on Running data and the Intern on Queued.
plan: Read the job table: what is queued and since when.
Start a worker to unblock the owner's jobs.
Make make dev supervise the worker itself.

decisions.decision: dev.py supervises the worker process itself instead of running it under the watchfiles command.
decisions.why: The watchfiles wrapper never ends, so dev.py's warning waited on it and a worker that died was never noticed or restarted.

decisions.decision: A worker that keeps failing waits longer before the next start (2 s doubling to 30 s), reset once it has run a minute.
decisions.why: A worker broken by a code error must not restart in a tight loop.

change: scripts/dev.py: supervise_worker (restart when the worker ends, with its exit code or signal; restart when a Python file under dclab_rnd changes), python_changed_since; tests/test_dev_script.py.

findings.defect: Stage runs and intern turns stayed queued after a build.
findings.scenario: make dev on PostgreSQL (DCLAB_WORKER=external): the worker ended about 90 seconds after start; four jobs queued for half an hour, the pages kept polling.
findings.cause: The worker ran under watchfiles, which restarts only on a file change; dev.py waited on watchfiles, not the worker, so its warning never fired. Why the worker ended is not in any record left (likely memory pressure while a test gate ran on the 8 GB machine).
findings.fix: dev.py runs and supervises the worker: an end is said with its exit code or the signal (SIGKILL named as the system short of memory) and the worker is started again; a code change restarts it.

findings.defect: The intern's models stage crawled once the worker was back.
findings.scenario: The store's hourly job (a whole store run, about twenty minutes of Python) ran in the same worker process as the owner's stage and intern turn.
findings.cause: Threads of one interpreter share its lock: a long pure-Python run slows every job beside it.
findings.fix: The store job runs python -m dclab_rnd.store run --agent-runs <home> in its own process at nice 10; a run without its record fails the job; the walks keeper opens a PostgreSQL workspace's stores itself.

measurements.name: the owner's queued jobs after a worker started
measurements.gate: every queued job is claimed and the project's stages move
measurements.result: the four queued jobs were claimed within seconds; the data stage completed; the intern turn ran

outcome: A make dev session can no longer leave jobs waiting for a worker that is gone.
lessons: Supervise the process that does the work, not a wrapper around it.
risks: A worker that dies for memory will die again under the same pressure; the restart only says it and tries again.
